cause_quote: In `captureGatewayToolCallerAssertion`, `return Object.assign(assertNotStopped, fences);` replaced the synchronous path that called `assertReceipt();`, bypassing the MCP loopback caller’s only check of the turn’s abort signal.
user_saw: After the user clicked Stop during a CLI-backed turn, a pending message action could still finish and write to the channel.
summary: The fix passes the CLI turn’s abort signal from the MCP loopback grant into the tool caller’s `approvalSignals`, restoring cancellation before a pending message action writes.
reasoning: I checked the parent of #203487 and confirmed that the loopback caller supplied its grant-currentness predicate as `receiptAuthority` and that the predicate returned false when the grant’s abort signal fired. The parent already contained an integration case that aborted during a reaction lookup and expected no write. The #203487 diff made the synchronous guard check only `approvalSignals`, which the loopback caller did not supply.
